lessons.title: Why, when and what to prune
lessons.html:
Why we prune shrubs

Pruning means cutting away parts of a plant on purpose. In gardens, parks and estates we prune shrubs to:

  • remove dead, diseased and damaged wood (the three Ds)
  • keep the shrub healthy, with good air flow inside
  • get more flowers or more leaves
  • keep a shape, such as a hedge or a ball (topiary)
  • keep paths, windows and signs clear

When to prune

Timing depends on when the shrub flowers. Get the timing wrong and you cut off next season's flowers.

Shrub typeWhen to pruneExamples
Flowers on new growthLate winter, before new growthRoses, plumbago, abelia
Flowers on old woodStraight after floweringAzalea, camellia, may (spiraea)
HedgesLight trims during the growing seasonDuranta, syzygium, murraya, spekboom

Your supervisor will tell you the schedule for your site. Dead, broken and diseased branches can be removed at any time.

Tools

  • Secateurs – stems up to about the thickness of a finger.
  • Loppers – thicker stems, with long handles.
  • Pruning saw – thick branches.
  • Hedge shears or hedge trimmer – for shaping hedges.

Keep tools sharp and clean. Blunt tools crush stems and let disease in. Wipe blades with a disinfectant between plants when cutting diseased wood.

lessons.title: Making good cuts and shaping
lessons.html:
How to make a good cut

  1. Find a healthy bud or side shoot facing outwards, the way you want the new growth to go.
  2. Cut about 5 mm above the bud, sloping away from it so rain runs off.
  3. Do not leave long stubs. Stubs die back and rot.
  4. Do not cut too close, or the bud will dry out.
  5. When removing a whole branch, cut just outside the collar (the swollen ring where it joins the main stem).

Thinning and heading back

  • Thinning – removing whole stems at the base or at a joint. This opens up the shrub and lets in light and air.
  • Heading back – shortening stems to a bud. This makes the shrub bushier.

Do not remove more than about one third of a shrub at one time unless your supervisor tells you to do a hard rejuvenation prune.

Shaping hedges

  • Use a string line and pegs to keep the top straight.
  • Make the base slightly wider than the top so light reaches the lower leaves. A hedge that is wider on top gets bare at the bottom.
  • Trim the sides first, then the top.

Cleaning up

Rake up clippings. Healthy material can go to the compost heap. Diseased material must be bagged and removed, not composted.

Safety

  • Wear gloves and eye protection. Hedge trimmers also need ear protection.
  • Check for wasps' nests, bees and snakes before you push into a shrub.
  • Use a stable ladder on firm ground; never stand on the top step. Never use powered trimmers above shoulder height from a ladder.
  • Keep the hedge trimmer cable behind you, or use a cordless one.

Key points

  • Always remove dead, diseased and damaged wood first.
  • Prune at the right time for the flowering type of the shrub.
  • Cut 5 mm above an outward-facing bud with a sloping cut; leave no stubs.
  • Keep hedges wider at the base than the top.
  • Use sharp, clean tools and the right PPE.
